metadata.title: Recursive Self-Improvement and the Binding Condition: A Formal Criterion for Lawful Improvement of Continuation Machinery
metadata.description: This preprint proposes a formal, auditable criterion for recursive self-improvement (RSI) under the binding-condition framework. It defines recursive self-improvement as lawful continuation improving the machinery of lawful continuation, where “lawful” denotes root-anchored authorization and satisfaction of governing binding conditions within a declared system boundary. The framework specifies a finite protected trust structure R -> H_t -> (C_t, E_t, V_t), in which a root authorization boundary anchors higher-order authorization, binding conditions, a protected evaluation vector, and a protected verifier. Improvement is vector-valued: at least one designated protected dimension must improve beyond a prespecified threshold, every protected dimension must remain within an explicit tolerance, and mandatory invariants must remain satisfied. Governance continuity requires changes to protected authority, conditions, evaluation criteria, or verifiers to remain root-authorized, declared before successor evaluation, reconstructable from preserved lineage, and incapable of granting retroactive certification. A transition constitutes self-improvement only when the current continuation machinery materially participates in producing its accepted update; RSI requires at least two consecutive accepted self-improvements, with the improved machinery materially participating in producing a subsequent accepted update. The paper provides five necessary principles, a ten-question binary decision procedure, a taxonomy distinguishing lawful RSI from ordinary learning, self-modification, AI-assisted improvement, recursive capability amplification, and recursive drift, and adversarial cases covering benchmark hacking, evaluator rewriting, criterion laundering, root replacement, authority laundering, and human-completed successor engineering. A prospective empirical protocol specifies pre-execution freezing of the root, system boundary, binding conditions, evaluation vector, verifier, causal participation rule, stopping and retry procedures, and evidence-sealing format, with complete preservation of proposals, tool calls, code changes, evaluations, verifier decisions, metadata, timestamps, state hashes, and failures. The paper does not demonstrate RSI in a deployed system, establish the moral legitimacy of a declared root, eliminate specification error, or claim that each component is individually novel; it proposes an integrated rooted criterion for determining when recursive capability change remains authorized, verifiable, condition-preserving, and materially recursive.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement and the Binding Condition: A Formal Criterion for Lawful Improvement of Continuation Machinery
